title.zh: 卷一百二十六 周書17: 列傳六 馮道
title.en: Volume 126 Book of Later Zhou 28: Biographies 6 - Feng Dao
title.raw: 卷一百二十六 周書17: 列傳六 馮道 Volume 126 Book of Later Zhou 28: Biographies 6 - Feng Dao

sentences.zh: 馮道，字可道，瀛州景城人。

translations.literal: Feng Dao, style name Kedao, was a native of Jingcheng in Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao, whose style was Kedao, came from Jingcheng in Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其先為農為儒，不恒其業。

translations.literal: His ancestors had been farmers and Confucian scholars, without a fixed occupation.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had tilled the fields and studied the classics by turns, never settling into a single livelihood.

sentences.zh: 道少純厚，好學能文，不恥惡衣食，負米奉親之外，惟以披誦吟諷為事，雖大雪擁戶，凝塵滿席，湛如也。

translations.literal: In youth Dao was pure and earnest, fond of learning and skilled in letters, not ashamed of poor food and clothing; apart from carrying rice to support his parents, he devoted himself solely to reading aloud and reciting in chant, and even when heavy snow blocked the doorway and dust lay thick on his mat, he remained serene.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man Feng Dao was guileless and diligent, devoted to study and adept at writing, and unashamed of coarse food and plain dress. Beyond carrying grain on his back to provide for his parents, he spent his days reading and reciting poetry; even when snow piled against the door and dust coated his mat, he remained perfectly at ease.

sentences.zh: 天祐中，劉守光署為幽州掾。

translations.literal: During the Tianyou era, Liu Shouguang appointed him an aide in You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianyou period Liu Shouguang appointed him a staff officer in Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 守光引兵伐中山，訪於僚屬，道常以利害箴之，守光怒，置於獄中，尋為人所救免。

translations.literal: When Shouguang led troops to attack Zhongshan and consulted his staff, Dao often admonished him on advantage and harm; Shouguang grew angry and imprisoned him, but before long someone secured his release.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouguang marched against Zhongshan and sought counsel from his officials, Dao repeatedly warned him of the risks and rewards involved. Shouguang flew into a rage and threw him in prison, but he was soon rescued and set free.

sentences.zh: 守光敗，遁歸太原，監軍使張承業辟為本院巡官。

translations.literal: After Shouguang was defeated, Dao fled to Taiyuan, where the army supervisor Zhang Chengye recruited him as an inspector of the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouguang fell, Dao made his way to Taiyuan, where Zhang Chengye, the military overseer, took him on as a headquarters inspector.

sentences.zh: 承業重其文章履行，甚見待遇。

translations.literal: Chengye valued his literary talent and conduct, and treated him with great favor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chengye admired both his literary gifts and his character, and showed him exceptional regard.

sentences.zh: 時有周元豹者，善人倫鑒，與道不洽，謂承業曰：「馮生無前程，公不可過用。

translations.literal: At the time there was a Zhou Yuanbao, skilled in judging men, who was on poor terms with Dao and said to Chengye, "Master Feng has no future prospects; you must not employ him too heavily.
translations.idiomatic: There was a man named Zhou Yuanbao, skilled at reading character, who disliked Dao and told Zhang Chengye, "Young Feng has no bright future ahead of him. You should not rely on him too heavily.

sentences.zh: 」時河東記室盧質聞之曰：「我曾見杜黃裳司空寫真圖，道之狀貌酷類焉，將來必副大用，元豹之言不足信也。

translations.literal: " At that time Lu Zhi of the Hedong secretariat heard this and said, "I once saw the portrait of Minister Du Huangshang; Dao's appearance closely resembles it, and in time he will surely be fit for great employment—Yuanbao's words are not to be trusted."
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Zhi of the Hedong secretariat overheard and said, "I once saw the portrait of Chief Minister Du Huangshang. Feng Dao's face is the very image of his. He is destined for high office, and Yuanbao's judgment cannot be trusted."

sentences.zh: 」承業尋薦為霸府從事，俄署太原掌書記，時莊宗並有河北，文翰甚繁，一以委之。

translations.literal: " Before long Chengye recommended him as an aide in the princely headquarters, and soon he was appointed chief secretary at Taiyuan; at that time Zhuangzong had united Hebei, official correspondence was extremely heavy, and all of it was entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Chengye soon recommended him as an aide in the princely headquarters, and shortly afterward appointed him chief secretary at Taiyuan. With Zhuangzong holding all of Hebei, the volume of official correspondence was immense, and Feng Dao handled all of it.

sentences.zh: 莊宗與梁軍夾河對壘，一日，郭崇韜以諸校伴食數多，主者不辦，請少罷減。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong faced the Liang army across the river; one day Guo Chongtao, because the number of officers sharing meals was too great for the steward to manage, asked that it be somewhat reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong's forces faced the Liang army across the Yellow River. One day Guo Chongtao noted that too many junior officers were dining together for the commissary to supply and asked that the number be cut back.

sentences.zh: 莊宗怒曰：「孤為效命者設食都不自由，其河北三鎮，令三軍別擇一人為帥，孤請歸太原以避賢路。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong angrily said, "I cannot even freely provide food for those who risk their lives for me! Let the three armies of the three Hebei circuits each choose a commander, and I shall return to Taiyuan to yield the path to worthies."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong burst out in anger: "I cannot even decide how to feed the men who die for me! Let each of the three armies in the three Hebei circuits pick its own commander. I will go back to Taiyuan and make way for better men."

sentences.zh: 」遽命道對面草詞，將示其眾。

translations.literal: " He immediately ordered Dao to draft a proclamation face to face, intending to show it to the troops.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered Feng Dao at once to draft a proclamation on the spot, intending to read it to the army.

sentences.zh: 道執筆久之，莊宗正色促焉，道徐起對曰：「道所掌筆硯，敢不供職。

translations.literal: Dao held the brush a long time; Zhuangzong, with stern countenance, urged him on. Dao rose slowly and replied, "The brush and ink I hold are my charge—how would I dare not perform my duty?
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao held his brush for a long while. Zhuangzong glared and pressed him. Dao rose slowly and said, "The brush and ink are in my charge. How could I fail to do my duty?

sentences.zh: 今大王屢集大功，方平南寇，崇韜所諫，未至過當，阻拒之則可，不可以向來之言，喧動群議，敵人若知，謂大王君臣之不和矣。

translations.literal: Now Your Highness has repeatedly achieved great merit and is on the verge of pacifying the southern foe; Chongtao's remonstrance was not excessive—refusing it would be enough; you must not, with words spoken in passion, stir up widespread debate, for if the enemy learns of it they will say that lord and minister are at odds."
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness has won victory after victory and is on the verge of crushing the southern enemy. Guo Chongtao's advice was not out of line. You may refuse it, but you must not, in a fit of anger, stir up the whole camp with words like these. If the enemy hears of it, they will think lord and minister are divided."

sentences.zh: 幸熟而思之，則天下幸甚也。

translations.literal: If you will ponder this carefully, it will be a great fortune for the realm."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Highness will think this through carefully, the realm will be greatly fortunate."

sentences.zh: 」俄而崇韜入謝，因道為之解焉，人始重其膽量。

translations.literal: " Before long Chongtao came in to apologize, and Dao interceded for him; only then did people begin to respect his courage.
translations.idiomatic: " Guo Chongtao soon came in to apologize, and Feng Dao spoke on his behalf. From that day men began to admire his nerve.

sentences.zh: 莊宗即位鄴宮，除省郎，充翰林學士，自綠衣賜紫。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne at the Ye palace, Dao was appointed a provincial bureau officer and made Hanlin academician, advancing from green robes to purple.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong assumed the throne at Ye, Feng Dao was made a bureau officer and Hanlin academician, promoted from the green robes of a junior official to purple.

sentences.zh: 梁平，遷中書舍人、戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Liang were pacified, he was transferred to Secretariat drafter and vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After the Liang were subdued, he was promoted to Secretariat drafter and vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，持服於景城。

translations.literal: Upon his father's death he entered mourning and observed the rites at Jingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he went into mourning and observed the full rites at home in Jingcheng.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （《談苑》：道聞父喪，即徒步見星以行，家人從後持衣囊追及之。）〉

translations.literal: (Tan Yuan: When Dao heard of his father's death, he set out on foot by starlight; his family followed behind with a bag of clothes and caught up with him.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Tan Yuan: On hearing of his father's death, Feng Dao set out on foot by starlight. His family followed with a bag of clothes and caught up with him.)]

sentences.zh: 遇歲儉，所得俸余悉賑於鄉里，道之所居惟蓬茨而已，凡牧宰饋遺，鬥粟匹帛無所受焉。

translations.literal: When the year was lean, he gave all surplus salary in relief to the neighborhood; where Dao lived was only a thatched hut, and from all prefectural and county officials who sent gifts he accepted not a peck of grain or a bolt of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of famine he gave every spare coin of his salary to his neighbors. His home was nothing but a thatched hut, and he refused every gift of grain or cloth sent by local officials.

sentences.zh: 時契丹方盛，素聞道名，欲掠而取之，會邊人有備，獲免。

translations.literal: At that time the Khitan were flourishing and had long heard of Dao's name; they wished to seize him, but because the border people were on guard he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan were then at the height of their power and had long heard of Feng Dao. They meant to capture him, but the border people were on alert and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 明宗入洛，遽謂近臣安重誨曰：「先帝時馮道郎中何在？

translations.literal: When Mingzong entered Luoyang, he abruptly asked his close adviser An Chonghui, "Where is Bureau Director Feng Dao from the former emperor's time?
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingzong entered Luoyang, he turned at once to his close adviser An Chonghui and asked, "Where is Bureau Director Feng Dao, who served under the late emperor?

sentences.zh: 」重誨曰：「近除翰林學士。

translations.literal: " Chonghui said, "He was recently appointed Hanlin academician."
translations.idiomatic: " An Chonghui replied, "He was recently made Hanlin academician."

sentences.zh: 」明宗曰：「此人朕素諳委，甚好宰相。

translations.literal: " Mingzong said, "This man I have long known and trusted—he would make an excellent chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: " Mingzong said, "I have known and trusted this man for years. He would make an excellent chief minister."

sentences.zh: 」俄拜端明殿學士，端明之號，自道始也。

translations.literal: " Before long he was appointed academician of the Hall of Illuminated Clarity—the title "Illuminated Clarity" began with Dao.
translations.idiomatic: " He was soon appointed academician of the Hall of Illuminated Clarity. The title itself began with Feng Dao.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷中書侍郎、刑部尚書、平章事。

translations.literal: Not long after, he was transferred to vice director of the Secretariat, minister of justice, and Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat, minister of justice, and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 凡孤寒士子，抱才業、素知識者皆與引用；

translations.literal: All poor scholars of talent whom he had long known he brought into employment;
translations.idiomatic: He promoted every poor scholar of talent he had long known;

sentences.zh: 唐末衣冠，履行浮躁者必抑而鎮之。

translations.literal: those among the late-Tang gentry whose conduct was frivolous he invariably restrained and subdued.
translations.idiomatic: and he invariably restrained and humbled those late-Tang gentlemen whose conduct was frivolous.

sentences.zh: 有工部侍郎任贊，因班退，與同列戲道於後曰：「若急行，必遺下《兔園冊》。

translations.literal: There was Ren Zan, vice minister of works, who after court dismissal jested behind Dao to his colleagues, saying, "If he walks fast, he is sure to drop his Garden of the Hare primer."
translations.idiomatic: Ren Zan, vice minister of works, once joked behind Feng Dao's back as court was dismissed: "If he hurries, he'll drop his Garden of the Hare primer."

sentences.zh: 」道知之，召贊謂曰：「《兔園冊》皆名儒所集，道能諷之，中朝士子止看文場秀句，便為舉業，皆竊取公聊，何淺狹之甚耶！

translations.literal: " When Dao learned of it, he summoned Zan and said, "The Garden of the Hare was compiled by famous Confucians—I can recite it from memory. Court scholars today read only clever lines from the examination field and call that their learning, all pilfering from high officials—how shallow and narrow!"
translations.idiomatic: " Feng Dao heard of it and summoned Ren Zan. "The Garden of the Hare was compiled by eminent scholars," he said. "I can recite it by heart. Court scholars today skim clever examination couplets and call that learning. They steal from their betters. How shallow can one be?"

sentences.zh: 」贊大愧焉。

translations.literal: " Zan was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: " Ren Zan was deeply ashamed.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （《歐陽史》云：《兔園策》者，鄉校俚儒教田夫牧子之所誦也。

translations.literal: (Ouyang's History says: The Garden of the Hare Primers were what village-school rustic teachers had farmers' sons recite.
translations.idiomatic: (Ouyang Xiu's History of the Five Dynasties says: The Garden of the Hare Primers were what rustic village teachers had farm boys memorize.

sentences.zh: 《北夢瑣言》云：《兔園策》乃徐、庾文體，非鄙樸之談，但家藏一本，人多賤之。

translations.literal: Beimeng Suoyan says: The Garden of the Hare Primers are in the style of Xu Ling and Yu Xin—not vulgar talk, yet though every household keeps a copy, most men despise it.
translations.idiomatic: Beimeng Suoyan says: The Garden of the Hare Primers are written in the style of Xu Ling and Yu Xin, not in crude prose, yet though every household keeps a copy, most men look down on it.

sentences.zh: 《困學紀聞》云：《兔園策府》三十卷，唐蔣王惲令僚佐杜嗣先仿應科目策，自設問對，引經史為訓註。

translations.literal: Kunxue Jiwen says: The Garden of the Hare Policy Treasury in thirty juan—Tang Prince Yun of Jiang ordered his aide Du Sixian to model it on examination policy questions, setting questions and answers himself and citing the classics and histories for commentary.
translations.idiomatic: Kunxue Jiwen says: The Garden of the Hare Policy Treasury, in thirty juan, was compiled when Tang Prince Yun of Jiang ordered his aide Du Sixian to imitate civil-service policy questions, framing questions and answers and citing the classics and histories in commentary.

sentences.zh: 惲，太宗子，故用梁王兔園名其書，馮道《兔園策》謂此也。）〉

translations.literal: Yun was a son of Taizong, hence he used the name of the Liang prince's Garden of the Hare for the book—Feng Dao's "Garden of the Hare Primers" refers to this.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Yun was a son of Emperor Taizong of Tang, hence the title drawn from the Liang prince's Garden of the Hare. Feng Dao's "Garden of the Hare Primers" refers to this work.)]

sentences.zh: 復有梁朝宰臣李琪，每以文章自擅，曾進《賀平中山王都表》云：「復真定之逆賊」。

translations.literal: There was also Li Qi, a Liang chief minister, who prided himself on his literary skill and once submitted a memorial congratulating the pacification of Zhongshan and Wang Du, saying, "We have recovered the rebel of Zhending."
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi, a chief minister of the Liang, also prided himself on his writing. He once submitted a memorial on the pacification of Zhongshan and Wang Du that read, "We have recovered the rebel of Zhending."

sentences.zh: 道讓琪曰：「昨來收復定州，非真定也。

translations.literal: Dao reproved Qi, saying, "What was recovered yesterday was Ding Prefecture, not Zhending."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao corrected him: "What was recovered was Dingzhou, not Zhending."

sentences.zh: 」琪昧於地理，頓至折角。

translations.literal: " Qi was ignorant of geography and was instantly put to rout.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Qi knew nothing of geography and was utterly humiliated.

sentences.zh: 其後百僚上明宗徽號凡三章，道自為之，其文渾然，非流俗之體，舉朝服焉。

translations.literal: Later, when the hundred officials presented three chapters of honorific titles for Mingzong, Dao wrote them himself; the text was unified and grand, not in a vulgar style, and the whole court admired it.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the officials presented three chapters of honorific titles for Mingzong, Feng Dao wrote them himself. The prose was seamless and elevated, far from the common run, and the whole court admired it.

sentences.zh: 道尤長於篇詠，秉筆則成，典麗之外，義含古道，必為遠近傳寫，故漸畏其高深，由是班行肅然，無澆漓之態。

translations.literal: Dao was especially skilled in verse; taking up the brush he would finish at once. Beyond elegance and splendor, his meaning held the ancient way, and his works were invariably copied near and far; thus men gradually feared his depth, and from this the court ranks grew solemn, without frivolous airs.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao excelled above all at poetry and prose. He took up the brush and finished at a stroke. Beyond elegance, his meaning held to the ancient way, and his work was copied far and wide. Men gradually stood in awe of his depth, and the court grew solemn, free of frivolity.

sentences.zh: 繼改門下侍郎、戶部吏部尚書、集賢殿弘文館大學士，加尚書左僕射，封始平郡公。

translations.literal: He was next made vice director of the Chancellery, minister of revenue and of personnel, grand academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and the Hongwen Institute, promoted to left vice director of the Department of State Affairs, and enfeoffed as Duke of Shiping.
translations.idiomatic: He was next made vice director of the Chancellery, minister of revenue and of personnel, grand academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and the Hongwen Institute, promoted to left vice director of the Department of State Affairs, and enfeoffed as Duke of Shiping.

sentences.zh: 一日，道因上謁既退，明宗顧謂侍臣曰：「馮道性純儉，頃在德勝寨居一茅庵，與從人同器食，臥則芻槁一束，其心晏如也。

translations.literal: One day, after Dao had paid his respects and withdrawn, Mingzong turned to his attendants and said, "Feng Dao is by nature pure and frugal. Not long ago at Desheng Stockade he lived in a thatched hut, ate from the same bowl as his followers, and slept on a single bundle of straw—yet his mind was perfectly at ease.
translations.idiomatic: One day, after Feng Dao had paid his respects and withdrawn, Mingzong said to his attendants, "Feng Dao is pure and frugal by nature. At Desheng Stockade he lived in a thatched hut, ate from the same bowl as his men, and slept on a bundle of straw, yet his mind was perfectly at ease.

sentences.zh: 及以父憂退歸鄉里，自耕樵采，與農夫雜處，略不以素貴介懷，真士大夫也。

translations.literal: When he withdrew to his home district in mourning for his father, he plowed, gathered firewood, and lived among farmers, scarcely letting his former status trouble him—a true gentleman."
translations.idiomatic: When he went home in mourning for his father, he plowed, gathered firewood, and lived among farmers without letting his former rank trouble him. He is a true gentleman."

sentences.zh: 」天成、長興中，天下屢稔，朝廷無事。

translations.literal: " In the Tiancheng and Changxing years the realm enjoyed repeated harvests and the court was untroubled.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tiancheng and Changxing reigns harvests were plentiful year after year and the court was at peace.

sentences.zh: 明宗每禦延英，留道訪以外事，道曰：「陛下以至德承天，天以有年表瑞，更在日慎一日，以答天心。

translations.literal: Mingzong whenever he held court at Yanying kept Dao to consult on outside affairs. Dao said, "Your Majesty, with supreme virtue receiving Heaven's mandate, Heaven shows abundant years as an auspice—you must be more careful day by day to answer Heaven's heart.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Mingzong held court at Yanying he kept Feng Dao to discuss affairs of state. Feng Dao said, "Your Majesty rules with supreme virtue and Heaven has sent years of plenty as a sign. You must be more careful with each passing day to answer Heaven's will.

sentences.zh: 臣每記在先皇霸府日，曾奉使中山，徑井陘之險，憂馬有蹶失，不敢怠於銜轡；

translations.literal: Your servant often recalls that in the days of the former emperor's princely headquarters, on a mission to Zhongshan I passed the peril of Jingxing Pass, fearing the horse might stumble, and dared not slacken the bit;
translations.idiomatic: I often recall that in the late emperor's days, on a mission to Zhongshan I crossed the peril of Jingxing Pass. I feared the horse might stumble and never slackened the reins.

sentences.zh: 及至平地，則無復持控，果為馬所顛仆，幾至於損。

translations.literal: when I reached level ground I no longer held control, and was indeed thrown by the horse, nearly coming to harm.
translations.idiomatic: Once I reached level ground I let go, and the horse threw me. I was nearly killed.

sentences.zh: 臣所陳雖小，可以喻大。

translations.literal: What your servant offers is small, but it may illustrate the large.
translations.idiomatic: What I say is a small matter, but it stands for a larger one.

sentences.zh: 陛下勿以清晏豐熟，便縱逸樂，兢兢業業，臣之望也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty must not, because the realm is peaceful and harvests abundant, give way to ease and pleasure—diligence and caution are what your servant hopes for."
translations.idiomatic: Do not, because the realm is peaceful and the harvest rich, give way to ease and pleasure. Diligence and caution are what I ask of you."

sentences.zh: 」明宗深然之。

translations.literal: " Mingzong deeply approved.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 他日又問道曰：「天下雖熟，百姓得濟否？

translations.literal: Another day he again asked Dao, "Though the realm has good harvests, are the common people provided for?
translations.idiomatic: On another day he asked Feng Dao, "The realm has good harvests, but are the people truly provided for?

sentences.zh: 」道曰：「穀貴餓農，穀賤傷農，此常理也。

translations.literal: " Dao said, "When grain is dear the farmer starves; when grain is cheap the farmer is ruined—this is the constant principle.
translations.idiomatic: " Feng Dao said, "When grain is dear the farmer starves; when grain is cheap the farmer is ruined. That is the constant law.

sentences.zh: 臣憶得近代有舉子聶夷中《傷田家詩》云：『二月賣新絲，五月糶秋穀。

translations.literal: Your servant recalls a recent examination candidate, Nie Yizhong, whose poem Lament for the Farm Household says: 'In the second month I sell the new silk; in the fifth month I pawn the autumn grain.
translations.idiomatic: I recall a recent candidate, Nie Yizhong, whose Lament for the Farm Household runs: "In the second month I sell the new silk; in the fifth month I pawn the autumn grain.

sentences.zh: 醫得眼下瘡，剜卻心頭肉。

translations.literal: To cure the sore before the eyes, I gouge out the flesh of the heart.'
translations.idiomatic: To cure the sore before my eyes, I gouge out the flesh of my heart."

sentences.zh: 我願君王心，化作光明燭。

translations.literal: 'I wish the ruler's heart might become a bright shining candle.
translations.idiomatic: "I wish the ruler's heart might become a bright shining candle,

sentences.zh: 不照綺羅筵，遍照逃亡屋。

translations.literal: Not shining on brocade banquets, but shining everywhere on the houses of the displaced.'"
translations.idiomatic: not shining on brocade banquets alone, but lighting every house of the displaced."

sentences.zh: 』」明宗曰：「此詩甚好。

translations.literal: Mingzong said, "This poem is excellent."
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong said, "That poem is excellent."

sentences.zh: 」遂命侍臣錄下，每自諷之。

translations.literal: " He then ordered his attendants to copy it down, and often recited it to himself.
translations.idiomatic: He had his attendants copy it down and often recited it to himself.

sentences.zh: 道之發言簡正，善於裨益，非常人所能及也。

translations.literal: Dao's words were concise and upright, skilled at benefit—beyond what ordinary men could reach.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao spoke with brevity and integrity and gave counsel of real benefit, beyond what ordinary men could offer.

sentences.zh: 時以諸經舛繆，與同列李愚委學官田敏等，取西京鄭覃所刊石經，雕為印版，流布天下，後進賴之。

translations.literal: At the time, because the classics were in error, he together with his colleague Li Yu commissioned the academic official Tian Min and others to take the stone classics engraved by Zheng Tan in the Western Capital, carve them into printing blocks, and circulate them through the realm—later students relied on this.
translations.idiomatic: Because the classics were full of errors, he and his colleague Li Yu commissioned the academic official Tian Min and others to take the stone classics engraved by Zheng Tan in the Western Capital, cut them into printing blocks, and circulate them through the realm. Later generations of scholars owed him a great debt.

sentences.zh: 明宗崩，唐末帝嗣位，以道為山陵使，禮畢，出鎮同州，循故事也。

translations.literal: When Mingzong died and the Last Tang Emperor succeeded, Dao was made director of the imperial tomb; when the rites were complete he was sent out to govern Tong Prefecture, following precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong died and the Last Tang Emperor succeeded, Feng Dao was made director of the imperial tomb. When the rites were complete he was posted to Tong Prefecture, following established precedent.

sentences.zh: 道為政閑淡，獄市無撓。

translations.literal: Dao's governance was easy and mild; prisons and markets were undisturbed.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was easy and mild. Prisons and markets were undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 一日，有上介胡饒，本出軍吏，性粗獷，因事詬道於牙門，左右數報不應。

translations.literal: One day a senior aide, Hu Rao, originally a military clerk, coarse by nature, on some pretext reviled Dao at the headquarters gate; attendants repeatedly reported it but he did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: One day a senior aide named Hu Rao, originally a military clerk and coarse by nature, reviled Feng Dao at the headquarters gate over some trifle. Attendants reported it repeatedly, but Feng Dao did not respond.

sentences.zh: 道曰：「此必醉耳！

translations.literal: Dao said, "He must be drunk!
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao said, "He must be drunk.

sentences.zh: 」因召入，開尊設食，盡夕而起，無撓慍之色。

translations.literal: " He then summoned him in, opened wine and set out food, and until evening they rose—without a trace of annoyance.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Hu Rao in, opened wine, and set out food. They sat together until evening without a trace of annoyance.

sentences.zh: 未幾，入為司空。

translations.literal: Before long he entered the capital as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled to the capital as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 及晉祖入洛，以道為首相。

translations.literal: When the Jin founder entered Luoyang, he made Dao chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin founder entered Luoyang, he made Feng Dao chief minister.

sentences.zh: 二年，契丹遣使加徽號於晉祖，晉祖亦獻徽號於契丹，謂道曰：「此行非卿不可。

translations.literal: In the second year the Khitan sent envoys to bestow an honorific title on the Jin founder, and the Jin founder also presented an honorific title to the Khitan; he said to Dao, "This mission cannot be undertaken without you."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the Khitan sent envoys to bestow an honorific title on the Jin founder, who in turn presented one to the Khitan. He told Feng Dao, "This mission cannot succeed without you."

sentences.zh: 」道無難色。

translations.literal: " Dao showed no difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao showed not the slightest hesitation.

sentences.zh: 晉祖又曰：「卿官崇德重，不可深入沙漠。

translations.literal: The Jin founder again said, "Your rank is lofty and your virtue weighty—you must not penetrate deep into the desert."
translations.idiomatic: The Jin founder added, "Your rank is high and your virtue great. You must not go deep into the desert."

sentences.zh: 」道曰：「陛下受北朝恩，臣受陛下恩，何有不可！」

translations.literal: " Dao said, "Your Majesty received favor from the northern court; your servant received favor from Your Majesty—how could there be anything impossible!"
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao replied, "Your Majesty received favor from the northern court. I received favor from Your Majesty. How could I refuse?"

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （楊內翰《談苑》云：道與諸相歸中書，食訖，外廳堂吏前白道言北使事。

translations.literal: (Hanlin Academician Yang's Tan Yuan says: Dao and the other chief ministers returned to the Secretariat; when the meal was finished, a clerk from the outer hall came forward to inform Dao of the northern envoy matter.
translations.idiomatic: (Hanlin Academician Yang's Tan Yuan says: Feng Dao and the other chief ministers returned to the Secretariat. When the meal was finished, a clerk from the outer hall came forward to inform him of the northern envoy mission.

sentences.zh: 吏人色變手戰，道取紙一幅，署云：「道去。

translations.literal: The clerk's face changed color and his hands trembled; Dao took a sheet of paper and wrote, "Dao goes."
translations.idiomatic: The clerk turned pale and his hands shook. Feng Dao took a sheet of paper and wrote, "Feng Dao goes."

sentences.zh: 」即遣寫敕進，堂吏泣下。

translations.literal: " He immediately had an edict drafted and submitted; the hall clerk wept.
translations.idiomatic: He had an edict drafted at once and submitted. The hall clerk wept.

sentences.zh: 道遣人語妻子，不復歸家，即日舍都亭驛，不數日北行。

translations.literal: Dao sent word to his wife and children that he would not return home; that same day he lodged at the Capital Pavilion post station, and within a few days set out north.
translations.idiomatic: He sent word to his wife and children that he would not come home, lodged that day at the Capital Pavilion post station, and within a few days set out north.

sentences.zh: 晉祖餞宴，語以家國之故，煩耆德遠使，自酌卮酒賜之，泣下。）〉

translations.literal: The Jin founder gave a farewell banquet, speaking of state and family and troubling his aged virtue with a distant mission; he poured a cup of wine himself and bestowed it, weeping.)〉
translations.idiomatic: The Jin founder gave a farewell banquet, spoke of state and family, and said he was troubling his aged virtue with so distant a mission. He poured a cup of wine with his own hand and gave it to him, weeping.)]

sentences.zh: 及行，將達西樓，契丹主欲郊迎，其臣曰：「天子無迎宰相之禮。

translations.literal: When he set out and was about to reach the Western Tower, the Khitan ruler wished to welcome him in the suburbs; his ministers said, "The Son of Heaven has no rite of welcoming a chief minister in the suburbs."
translations.idiomatic: As he traveled and was about to reach the Western Tower, the Khitan ruler wished to welcome him in the suburbs. His ministers said, "The Son of Heaven has no rite of going out to welcome a chief minister."

sentences.zh: 」因止焉，其名動殊俗也如此。

translations.literal: " They therefore stopped him—such was the way his name stirred foreign peoples.
translations.idiomatic: They stopped him. Such was the way his name stirred foreign peoples.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （《談苑》云：契丹賜其臣牙笏及臘日賜牛頭者為殊禮，道皆得之，作詩以紀曰：「牛頭偏得賜，象笏更容持。

translations.literal: (Tan Yuan says: Among the Khitan, bestowing ivory tablets on ministers and giving ox heads on the La festival day were special honors—Dao received them all, and composed a poem to record it: "Ox head uniquely bestowed, ivory tablet yet allowed to hold."
translations.idiomatic: (Tan Yuan says: Among the Khitan, ivory tablets for ministers and ox heads on the La festival were special honors. Feng Dao received them all and wrote a poem: "Ox head uniquely bestowed, ivory tablet yet allowed to hold."

sentences.zh: 」契丹主甚喜，遂潛諭留意，道曰：「南朝為子，北朝為父，兩朝皆為臣，豈有分別哉！

translations.literal: " The Khitan ruler was greatly pleased and secretly instructed him to take heed; Dao said, "The southern court is son, the northern court is father—both courts are my lords; how could there be any distinction!"
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler was greatly pleased and secretly urged him to stay. Feng Dao said, "The southern court is son, the northern court is father. I am subject to both. How can there be any distinction?"

sentences.zh: 」道在契丹，凡得所賜，悉以市薪炭，征其意，云：「北地苦寒，老年所不堪，當為之備。

translations.literal: " While Dao was among the Khitan, whatever he received in gifts he used entirely to buy fuel and charcoal, revealing his intent, saying, "The northern land is bitterly cold; old age cannot bear it—I must prepare."
translations.idiomatic: While among the Khitan, whatever gifts he received he spent entirely on fuel and charcoal, revealing his intent: "The north is bitterly cold. Old age cannot bear it. I must prepare."

sentences.zh: 」若將久留者。

translations.literal: " As if he would stay long.
translations.idiomatic: As if he meant to stay for good.

sentences.zh: 契丹感其意，乃遣歸，道三上表乞留，固遣乃去，猶更住館中月餘。

translations.literal: The Khitan were moved by his intent and sent him back; Dao thrice submitted memorials begging to remain, but they firmly sent him away—yet he still stayed in the guest lodge more than a month longer.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan were moved and sent him back. Feng Dao submitted three memorials begging to stay, but they firmly sent him away. He still lingered in the guest lodge for more than a month.

sentences.zh: 既行，所至留駐，凡兩月方出境，左右語道曰：「當北土得生還，恨無羽翼，公獨宿留，何也？

translations.literal: Once he set out, wherever he went he lingered; only after two months did he leave their territory. Those about him said to Dao, "In the northern land, to gain life and return, one regrets having no wings—yet you alone delay. Why?"
translations.idiomatic: Once he set out he lingered wherever he went and took two months to leave their territory. His attendants said, "In the north, to escape alive one wishes for wings. Yet you alone delay. Why?"

sentences.zh: 」道曰：「縱急還，彼以筋腳馬，一夕即追及，亦何可脫，但徐緩即不能測矣。

translations.literal: " Dao said, "Even if we hurry back, they have swift horses and would overtake us in a single night—how could we escape? Only by going slowly can they not gauge our intent."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao said, "Even if we hurry, they have swift horses and would overtake us in a night. How could we escape? Only by going slowly can they not guess our intent."

sentences.zh: 」眾乃服。

translations.literal: " The company then submitted.
translations.idiomatic: His companions were convinced.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，始至京師。）〉

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year he finally reached the capital.)〉
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year he finally reached the capital.)]

sentences.zh: 及還，朝廷廢樞密使，依唐朝故事，並歸中書，其院印付道，事無巨細，悉以歸之。

translations.literal: When he returned, the court abolished the Bureau of Military Affairs; following Tang precedent, its functions all reverted to the Secretariat, and its seal was given to Dao—matters great and small all passed to him.
translations.idiomatic: On his return the court abolished the Bureau of Military Affairs. Following Tang precedent, its functions reverted to the Secretariat, and its seal was given to Feng Dao. Matters great and small all passed through his hands.

sentences.zh: 尋加司徒、兼侍中，進魯國公。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Minister of Education and concurrent Palace Secretary, advanced to Duke of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Minister of Education and concurrent Palace Secretary and advanced to Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 晉祖曾以用兵事問道，道曰：陛下歷試諸艱，創成大業，神武睿略，為天下所知，討伐不庭，須從獨斷。

translations.literal: The Jin founder once asked Dao about military affairs. Dao said, "Your Majesty has passed through every hardship and founded a great enterprise; divine martial prowess and wise strategy are known throughout the realm—punishing the rebellious must follow Your Majesty's sole decision.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin founder once asked Feng Dao about military affairs. Feng Dao said, "Your Majesty has passed through every hardship and founded a great enterprise. Your divine martial prowess and wise strategy are known throughout the realm. Punishing the rebellious must be Your Majesty's sole decision.

sentences.zh: 臣本自書生，為陛下在中書，守歷代成規，不敢有一毫之失也。

translations.literal: Your servant was originally a bookish man; serving Your Majesty in the Secretariat, I keep the established rules of successive dynasties and dare not permit a single hair's breadth of error.
translations.idiomatic: I was originally a scholar. Serving Your Majesty in the Secretariat, I keep the established rules of successive dynasties and dare not permit the slightest error.

sentences.zh: 臣在明宗朝，曾以戎事問臣，臣亦以斯言答之。

translations.literal: In Mingzong's court, when military affairs were asked of your servant, your servant also answered with these words.
translations.idiomatic: In Mingzong's court, when military affairs were asked of me, I answered with these same words.

sentences.zh: 」晉祖頗可其說。

translations.literal: " The Jin founder greatly approved his statement.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin founder greatly approved.

sentences.zh: 道嘗上表求退，晉祖不之覽，先遣鄭王就省，謂曰：「卿來日不出，朕當親行請卿。

translations.literal: Dao once submitted a memorial requesting retirement; the Jin founder did not read it, but first sent the Prince of Zheng to visit him, saying, "If you do not come out tomorrow, I shall go in person to request you."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao once submitted a memorial requesting retirement. The Jin founder did not read it but sent the Prince of Zheng to visit him, saying, "If you do not come out tomorrow, I shall go in person to fetch you."

sentences.zh: 」道不得已出焉。

translations.literal: " Dao had no choice but to go out.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao had no choice but to appear.

sentences.zh: 當時寵遇，無與為比。

translations.literal: At that time the favor shown him had no equal.
translations.idiomatic: No one in that age was favored as he was.

sentences.zh: 晉少帝即位，加守太尉，進封燕國公。

translations.literal: When the Jin Lesser Emperor succeeded, Dao was made acting Grand Marshal and advanced to Duke of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin Lesser Emperor succeeded, Feng Dao was made acting Grand Marshal and enfeoffed as Duke of Yan.

sentences.zh: 道嘗問朝中熟客曰：「道之在政事堂，人有何說？

translations.literal: Dao once asked a familiar guest at court, "What do people say about Dao in the Secretariat?
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao once asked a court acquaintance, "What do people say about me in the Secretariat?

sentences.zh: 」客曰：「是非相半。

translations.literal: " The guest said, "Praise and blame are evenly divided."
translations.idiomatic: The man replied, "Praise and blame are about equal."

sentences.zh: 」道曰：「凡人同者為是，不同為非，而非道者，十恐有九。

translations.literal: " Dao said, "Ordinary men call agreement right and disagreement wrong—those who find fault with Dao are probably nine in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao said, "Ordinary men call agreement right and disagreement wrong. Those who find fault with me are probably nine in ten.

sentences.zh: 昔仲尼聖人也，猶為叔孫武叔所毀，況道之虛薄者乎！

translations.literal: In antiquity Confucius was a sage, yet he was still slandered by Shusun Wushu—how much more one as empty and slight as Dao!
translations.idiomatic: Confucius was a sage, yet Shusun Wushu slandered him. How much more should a man as slight as I expect it!

sentences.zh: 」然道之所持，始終不易。

translations.literal: " Yet what Dao held to, from beginning to end he did not change.
translations.idiomatic: Yet what I hold to, I have never changed from first to last.

sentences.zh: 後有人間道於少帝曰：「道好平時宰相，無以濟其艱難，如禪僧不可呼鷹耳！

translations.literal: Later someone slandered Dao to the Lesser Emperor, saying, "Dao is suited to be chief minister in peaceful times but cannot meet hardship—like a Chan monk who cannot call hawks!"
translations.idiomatic: Later someone slandered Feng Dao to the Lesser Emperor: "He is a chief minister for peaceful times but useless in crisis, like a Chan monk who cannot call hawks!"

sentences.zh: 」由是出道為同州節度使。

translations.literal: " On this account Dao was sent out as military governor of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On this account Feng Dao was posted out as military governor of Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，移鎮南陽，加中書令。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to garrison Nanyang and made Palace Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was transferred to Nanyang and made Palace Secretary.

sentences.zh: 契丹入汴，道自襄、鄧召入，戎王因從容問曰：「天下百姓，如何可救？

translations.literal: When the Khitan entered Bian, Dao was summoned from Xiang and Deng; the barbarian ruler casually asked, "How can the common people of the realm be saved?
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan entered Bian, Feng Dao was summoned from Xiang and Deng. The Khitan ruler asked at ease, "How can the people of the realm be saved?

sentences.zh: 」道曰：「此時百姓，佛再出救不得，惟皇帝救得。

translations.literal: " Dao said, "At this time, even if the Buddha were reborn he could not save the people—only the emperor can save them."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao said, "At this hour, even if the Buddha were reborn he could not save them. Only the emperor can."

sentences.zh: 」其後衣冠不至傷夷，皆道與趙延壽陰護之所至也。

translations.literal: " After this the gentry and officials were not harmed—all owing to the secret protection of Dao and Zhao Yanshou.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the gentry and officials were spared harm, thanks to the secret protection of Feng Dao and Zhao Yanshou.

sentences.zh: 是歲三月，隨契丹北行，與晉室公卿俱抵常山。

translations.literal: In the third month of that year he followed the Khitan north, reaching Changshan together with the Jin court nobles and officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of that year he followed the Khitan north and reached Changshan with the Jin court nobles and officials.

sentences.zh: 俄而比主卒，永康王代統其眾。

translations.literal: Before long the northern ruler died and Prince Yongkang took command of his forces.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Khitan emperor died and Prince Yongkang took command of the army.

sentences.zh: 及北去，留其族嘉裏以據常山。

translations.literal: When they went north they left their clansman Jiali to hold Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: As they marched north they left their clansman Jiali to hold Changshan.

sentences.zh: 時漢軍憤激，因共逐出嘉裏，尋復其城。

translations.literal: At that time the Han troops were inflamed with anger and together drove out Jiali, soon recovering the city.
translations.idiomatic: The Han troops were furious and together drove out Jiali, soon recovering the city.

sentences.zh: 道率同列四出按撫，因事從宜，各安其所。

translations.literal: Dao led his colleagues in four directions to pacify and reassure, adapting measures to circumstances so that each found his place.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao led his colleagues in four directions to pacify the people, adapting measures to circumstances until each man was settled.

sentences.zh: 人或推其功，道曰：「儒臣何能為，皆諸將之力也。

translations.literal: When some attributed the merit to him, Dao said, "What can a Confucian minister do? It was all the generals' strength.
translations.idiomatic: When some credited him with the victory, Feng Dao said, "What can a scholar-official do? It was all the generals' doing.

sentences.zh: 」道以德重，人所取則，乃為眾擇諸將之勤宿者，以騎校白再榮權為其帥，軍民由是帖然，道首有力焉。

translations.literal: " Dao, for the weight of his virtue, was what people took as their standard. He then chose among the generals those who were diligent and long-serving, and made Cavalry Commandant Bai Zairong provisional commander. Thereby military and civilian alike became settled, and Dao was foremost in this.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao carried such moral authority that men held him up as their model. He picked out the hardest-working, most seasoned of the generals and installed Cavalry Commandant Bai Zairong as provisional commander. Army and populace settled at once, and Feng Dao was the driving force.

sentences.zh: 道在常山，見有中國士女為契丹所俘者，出橐裝以贖之，皆寄於高尼精舍，後相次訪其家以歸之。

translations.literal: When Dao was at Changshan, he saw Chinese men and women taken captive by the Khitan. He spent from his own purse to ransom them, lodged them all at a Buddhist nunnery, and later, one after another, sought out their families to return them home.
translations.idiomatic: While at Changshan, Feng Dao saw Chinese men and women seized by the Khitan. He paid from his own funds to ransom them, placed them in a Buddhist nunnery, and later tracked down their families one by one and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 又，契丹先留道與李崧、和凝及文武官等在常山，是歲閏七月二十九日，契丹有詔追崧，令選朝士十人赴木葉山行事。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Khitan had earlier left Dao at Changshan with Li Song, He Ning, and the civil and military officials. That year, on the twenty-ninth day of the intercalary seventh month, the Khitan issued an edict summoning Song and ordering the selection of ten court scholars to go to Muye Mountain to perform rites.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan had earlier left Feng Dao at Changshan together with Li Song, He Ning, and the civil and military officials. That year, on the twenty-ninth day of the intercalary seventh month, they issued an edict recalling Song and ordering ten court scholars chosen to go to Muye Mountain on official business.

sentences.zh: 契丹麻答召道等至帳所，欲諭之，崧偶先至，知其意，懼形於色。

translations.literal: The Khitan Mada summoned Dao and the others to his tent, intending to inform them. Song happened to arrive first, understood their purpose, and fear showed on his face.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan prince Mada summoned Feng Dao and the others to his tent to explain matters. Li Song happened to arrive first, grasped what was intended, and could not keep fear from his face.

sentences.zh: 契丹麻答將以明日與朝士齊遣之，崧乃不俟道，與凝先出，既而相遇於帳門之外，因與分手俱歸。

translations.literal: Mada intended to send them off together with the court scholars the next day. Song therefore did not wait for Dao, but left first with He Ning. Presently they met outside the tent gate, then parted and each returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Mada meant to dispatch them together with the court scholars the following day. Li Song did not wait for Feng Dao, but left first with He Ning. They ran into each other outside the tent gate, then parted and went their separate ways home.

sentences.zh: 俄而李筠等縱火與契丹交鬥，鼓槊相及。

translations.literal: Before long Li Jun and others set fires and fought the Khitan; drums and spears clashed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Jun and his men set fires and battled the Khitan, drums beating and spears crossing.

sentences.zh: 是日若齊至，與麻答相見，稍或躊躇，則悉為俘矣。

translations.literal: If on that day they had all arrived together, met Mada, and shown even the slightest hesitation, they would all have been taken captive.
translations.idiomatic: Had they all arrived together that day, met Mada, and betrayed even a moment's hesitation, every one of them would have been taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 時論者以道布衣有至行，立公朝有重望，其陰報昭感，多此類也。

translations.literal: Commentators of the time held that Dao, though a commoner in dress, possessed supreme conduct and, once established at court, enjoyed great repute; his hidden rewards and manifest gratitude took many such forms.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries held that Feng Dao, for all his plain dress, possessed supreme integrity and, once he stood at court, commanded great respect. Hidden heaven-sent rewards of this kind were many.

sentences.zh: 及自常山入覲，漢祖嘉之，拜守太師。

translations.literal: When he came from Changshan to audience, the Han Founder praised him and appointed him Grand Preceptor, which he retained.
translations.idiomatic: When he came from Changshan to pay court, the Han Founder commended him and appointed him Grand Preceptor.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （《洛陽搢紳舊聞記》：贈大監張公璨，漢祖即位之初為上黨戎判。

translations.literal: (Old Stories Among the Gentry of Luoyang: Grand Supervisor Zhang Gongcan, posthumously ennobled, served at the beginning of the Han Founder's reign as military judge of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: (Old Stories Among the Gentry of Luoyang: Zhang Gongcan, posthumously titled Grand Supervisor, served at the outset of the Han Founder's reign as military judge of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 漢祖在北京時，大聚甲兵，禁牛皮不得私貿易及民間盜用之，如有牛死，即時官納其皮，其有犯者甚眾。

translations.literal: When the Han Founder was at the Northern Capital, he greatly gathered armor and troops and forbade private trade in oxhide and its unauthorized use among the people. If an ox died, its hide had at once to be turned in to the government. Those who violated the ban were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: While the Han Founder was still at the Northern Capital, he massed armor and troops and banned private trade in oxhide and its unauthorized use among the people. Any ox that died had to have its hide surrendered to the government at once. Violations were widespread.

sentences.zh: 及即大位，三司舉行請禁天下牛皮法，與河東時同，天下苦之。

translations.literal: When he assumed the throne, the Three Departments proposed implementing the nationwide oxhide ban, the same as in Hedong, and all under Heaven suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: Once he took the throne, the Department of State Affairs proposed extending the oxhide ban nationwide, identical to the Hedong rule, and the realm groaned under it.

sentences.zh: 會上黨民犯牛皮者二十餘人，獄成，罪俱當死。

translations.literal: It happened that more than twenty people in Shangdang violated the oxhide ban. When the case was closed, all were liable to death.
translations.idiomatic: More than twenty people in Shangdang were caught violating the oxhide ban. When judgment was rendered, all were sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 大監時為判官，獨執曰：「主上欽明，三司不合如此起請，二十餘人死尚間可，使天下犯者皆銜冤而死乎！

translations.literal: The Grand Supervisor, then serving as judge, alone held firm and said, "Our lord is discerning and wise. The Three Departments ought not to have submitted such a proposal. That more than twenty should die might still be tolerable—but are all violators under Heaven to die bearing grievance!
translations.idiomatic: Grand Supervisor Zhang, then serving as judge, alone stood firm and said, "Our lord is discerning and wise. The Three Departments should never have submitted such a proposal. That more than twenty men should die might still be borne—but shall every violator in the realm die with a grievance on his lips?

sentences.zh: 且主上在河東，大聚甲兵，須藉牛皮，嚴禁可也，今為天下君，何少牛皮，立法至於此乎！

translations.literal: Moreover, when our lord was in Hedong, he greatly gathered armor and troops and needed oxhide; a strict ban was fitting. Now he is lord of all under Heaven—what shortage of oxhide is there, that the law should be pushed this far!
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty was in Hedong, you massed armor and troops and had need of oxhide—a strict ban was understandable. But now you are sovereign of the realm. What lack of oxhide could justify pushing the law this far?

sentences.zh: 」遂封奏之。

translations.literal: " He thereupon sealed and memorialized it.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon sealed the memorial and submitted it.

sentences.zh: 時三司使方用事，執政之地，除馮瀛王外皆惡之，曰：「豈有州郡使敢非朝廷詔敕！

translations.literal: At the time the Three Departments commissioners were in power at the seat of government. Apart from Prince of Ying Feng, all hated him and said, "How can a prefectural commissioner dare oppose an imperial edict of the court!
translations.idiomatic: The Three Departments commissioners then held sway at court. Everyone except Prince of Ying Feng resented him and said, "How dare a circuit commissioner oppose an imperial edict of the court!

sentences.zh: 」力言於漢祖。

translations.literal: " They pressed their case before the Han Founder.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed their case hard before the Han Founder.

sentences.zh: 漢祖亦怒曰：「昭義一判官，是何敢如此！

translations.literal: The Han Founder also grew angry and said, "A mere judge of Zhaoyi—how dare he act thus!
translations.idiomatic: The Han Founder was furious as well. "One judge in Zhaoyi—who is he to behave like this!

sentences.zh: 其犯牛皮者，依敕俱死。

translations.literal: Those who violated the oxhide ban shall all die according to the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The oxhide violators shall all die as the edict commands.

sentences.zh: 大監以非毀詔敕，亦死。

translations.literal: The Grand Supervisor, for denigrating the edict, shall also die.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Supervisor Zhang, for denigrating the edict, shall die as well.

sentences.zh: 」敕未下，獨瀛王非時請見。

translations.literal: " Before the edict was issued, the Prince of Ying alone requested an unscheduled audience.
translations.idiomatic: Before the edict could be issued, Prince of Ying Feng alone requested an unscheduled audience.

sentences.zh: 漢祖出，瀛王曰：「陛下在河東時，斷牛皮可也，今既有天下，牛皮不合禁。

translations.literal: The Han Founder came out, and the Prince of Ying said, "When Your Majesty was in Hedong, banning oxhide was permissible. Now that you hold all under Heaven, oxhide ought not to be banned.
translations.idiomatic: The Han Founder came out, and Prince of Ying Feng said, "When Your Majesty was in Hedong, banning oxhide was defensible. Now that you hold the realm, oxhide should not be banned.

sentences.zh: 陛下赤子枉死之，亦足為陛下惜。

translations.literal: That Your Majesty's own people should die unjustly is itself enough to grieve Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: That Your Majesty's own people should die unjustly is grief enough for any sovereign.

sentences.zh: 昭義判官，以卑位食陛下祿，居陛下官，不惜軀命，敢執而奏之，可賞不可殺。

translations.literal: The Zhaoyi judge, though in a low post, eats Your Majesty's salary and holds Your Majesty's office. He did not spare his life but dared to hold firm and memorialize—he should be rewarded, not killed.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhaoyi judge holds a humble post, yet he eats Your Majesty's salary and fills Your Majesty's office. He risked his life to stand firm and memorialize. He deserves reward, not execution.

sentences.zh: 臣當輔弼之任，使此敕枉害天下人性命，臣不能早奏，使陛下正，臣罪當誅。

translations.literal: Your servant bears the duty of assisting and supporting. That this edict would wrongly harm the lives of people under Heaven—your servant failed to memorialize early and set Your Majesty right. Your servant's crime deserves death.
translations.idiomatic: I bear the duty of assisting Your Majesty. That this edict would wrongly cost lives across the realm—I failed to speak up in time and set Your Majesty on the right course. My own offense deserves death.

sentences.zh: 」稽首再拜。

translations.literal: " He bowed his head and prostrated himself twice.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed his head to the ground twice.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「張璨不合加罪，望加敕赦之。

translations.literal: He also said, "Zhang Can ought not to be punished. I beg that an edict be added to pardon him.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Zhang Can should not be punished. I beg Your Majesty to issue an edict pardoning him.

sentences.zh: 」漢祖久之曰：「已行之矣。

translations.literal: " After a long silence the Han Founder said, "It has already been done.
translations.idiomatic: After a long silence the Han Founder said, "It is already done.

sentences.zh: 」馮瀛王曰：「敕未下。

translations.literal: " The Prince of Ying Feng said, "The edict has not yet been issued.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Ying Feng said, "The edict has not yet gone out.

sentences.zh: 」漢祖遽曰：「與赦之。

translations.literal: " The Han Founder hastily said, "Then pardon him.
translations.idiomatic: The Han Founder said at once, "Then pardon him.

sentences.zh: 」馮曰：「勒停可乎？

translations.literal: " Feng said, "Would ordering it halted suffice?
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao asked, "Would ordering it halted suffice?

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「可。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said, "It will do.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Yes.

sentences.zh: 」由是改其敕，記其略曰：「三司邦計，國法攸依，張璨體事未明，執理乖當，宜停見職，犯牛皮者貸命放之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the edict was revised. Its gist read: "The Three Departments oversee the state's finances; national law rests upon them. Zhang Can did not grasp the matter clearly and handled the principle improperly. He should be removed from his present office. Those who violated the oxhide ban are spared death and released.
translations.idiomatic: The edict was revised accordingly. Its gist read: "The Three Departments oversee the state's finances, and national law rests upon them. Zhang Can did not grasp the matter clearly and handled the principle improperly. He is removed from his present office. The oxhide violators are spared and released.

sentences.zh: 」大監聽宣敕訖，聞敕云「執理乖當」，尚曰：「中書自不能執理，若一一教外道判官執理，則焉用彼相乎！」）〉

translations.literal: " When the Grand Supervisor had heard the edict proclaimed, he heard the edict say "handled the principle improperly," and still said, "If the Secretariat itself cannot handle principle properly, and must teach every outside circuit judge to do so, what use are those chief ministers!" )〉
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Supervisor Zhang heard the edict read aloud and caught the phrase "handled the principle improperly," he still remarked, "If the Secretariat cannot handle principle on its own and must teach every circuit judge outside the capital to do it for them, what good are those chief ministers?" )〉

sentences.zh: 乾祐中，道奉朝請外，平居自適。

translations.literal: During the Qianyou era, apart from his honorary court attendance, Dao lived quietly at his ease.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianyou era, apart from his honorary court attendance, Feng Dao lived quietly at his ease.

sentences.zh: 一日，著《長樂老自敘》云：

translations.literal: One day he composed An Autobiographical Account of the Old Man of Changle, which reads:
translations.idiomatic: One day he wrote An Autobiographical Account of the Old Man of Changle, which begins:

sentences.zh: 余世家宗族，本始平、長樂二郡，歷代之名實，具載於國史家牒。

translations.literal: My clan is an old established family; our ancestral home was Shiping and Changle prefectures. The names and deeds of each generation are fully recorded in the national histories and family registers.
translations.idiomatic: My clan is an old established family, originally from Shiping and Changle prefectures. The names and deeds of each generation are fully recorded in the national histories and our family registers.

sentences.zh: 余先自燕亡歸晉，事莊宗、明宗、閔帝、清泰帝，又事晉高祖皇帝、少帝。

translations.literal: My forebears fled Yan and returned to Jin, serving Zhuangzong, Mingzong, the Min Emperor, and the Qingtai Emperor, and also serving Emperor Gaozu of Jin and the Young Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: My forebears fled Yan and returned to Jin, serving Zhuangzong, Mingzong, the Min Emperor, and the Qingtai Emperor, and also Emperor Gaozu of Jin and the Young Emperor.

sentences.zh: 契丹據汴京，為北主所制，自鎮州與文武臣僚、馬步將士歸漢朝，事高祖皇帝、今上。

translations.literal: When the Khitan occupied Bianjing, I was controlled by the northern ruler; from Zhenzhou, together with civil and military officials and mounted and infantry troops, I returned to the Han court and served Emperor Gaozu and the present sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan held Bianjing, I was subject to their northern ruler. From Zhenzhou I returned to the Han court with civil and military officials and cavalry and infantry troops, and served Emperor Gaozu and the reigning sovereign.

sentences.zh: 顧以久叨祿位，備歷艱危，上顯祖宗，下光親戚。

translations.literal: Reflecting that I have long enjoyed salary and rank, having endured every hardship and danger, to bring glory to my ancestors above and honor to my kin below.
translations.idiomatic: When I consider how long I have held office and salary, and how many hardships and dangers I have passed through, I hope to bring honor to my ancestors above and credit to my relatives below.

sentences.zh: 亡曾祖諱湊，累贈至太傅，亡曾祖母崔氏，追封梁國太夫人；

translations.literal: My deceased great-grandfather, taboo name Cou, was posthumously promoted by successive grants to Grand Preceptor; my deceased great-grandmother, the Lady Cui, was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Madame of the State of Liang;
translations.idiomatic: My late great-grandfather, whose taboo name was Cou, was repeatedly promoted posthumously until he reached Grand Preceptor; my late great-grandmother, Lady Cui, was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Madame of the State of Liang;

sentences.zh: 亡祖諱炯，累贈至太師，亡祖母褚氏，追封吳國太夫人；

translations.literal: My deceased grandfather, taboo name Jiong, was posthumously promoted by successive grants to Grand Preceptor; my deceased grandmother, the Lady Chu, was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Madame of the State of Wu;
translations.idiomatic: My late grandfather, whose taboo name was Jiong, was repeatedly promoted posthumously until he reached Grand Preceptor; my late grandmother, Lady Chu, was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Madame of the State of Wu;

sentences.zh: 亡父諱良建，秘書少監致仕，累贈至尚書令，母張氏，追封魏國太夫人。

translations.literal: My deceased father, taboo name Liangjian, retired as Vice Director of the Secretariat and was posthumously promoted by successive grants to Director of the Department of State Affairs; my mother, the Lady Zhang, was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Madame of the State of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: My late father, whose taboo name was Liangjian, retired as Vice Director of the Secretariat and was repeatedly promoted posthumously until he reached Director of the Department of State Affairs; my mother, Lady Zhang, was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Madame of the State of Wei.

sentences.zh: 余階自將仕郎，轉朝議郎、朝散大夫、銀青光祿大夫、金紫光祿大夫、特進、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: As for my rank, I began as Gentleman for Merit, and was transferred through Gentleman for Court Discussion, Grand Master for Court Discussion, Grand Master with Silver-Green Seal and Glorious Emolument, Grand Master with Purple-Gold Seal and Glorious Emolument, Special Advancement, and Grand Master of the Palace with the Same Three Departments of State.
translations.idiomatic: In rank I rose from Gentleman for Merit through Gentleman for Court Discussion, Grand Master for Court Discussion, Grand Master with Silver-Green Seal and Glorious Emolument, Grand Master with Purple-Gold Seal and Glorious Emolument, Special Advancement, and Grand Master of the Palace with the Same Three Departments of State.

sentences.zh: 職自幽州節度巡官、河東節度巡官、掌書記，再為翰林學士，改授端明殿學士、集賢殿大學士、太微宮使，再為宏文館大學士，又充諸道鹽鐵轉運使、南郊大禮使、明宗皇帝晉高祖皇帝山陵使，再授定國軍節度、同州管內觀察處置等使，一為長春宮使，又授武勝軍節度、鄧隨均房等州管內觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: As for my posts, I began as an inspection officer of the Youzhou military governorship and an inspection officer of the Hedong military governorship, and as chief secretary; twice I served as Hanlin academician; I was then appointed academician of the Hall of Illuminated Clarity, grand academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and commissioner of the Taewei Palace; again I served as grand academician of the Hongwen Hall; I also served as commissioner for salt and iron transport of all circuits, commissioner for the southern suburbs grand rites, and imperial tomb commissioner for Emperors Mingzong and Gaozu of Jin; I was again appointed military governor of the Dingguo Army and commissioner for observation and disposition within Tong Prefecture and the like; once I served as commissioner of the Changchun Palace; and I was again appointed military governor of the Wusheng Army and commissioner for observation and disposition within Deng, Sui, Jun, Fang, and other prefectures and the like.
translations.idiomatic: In office I began as an inspection officer under the Youzhou and Hedong military governors and as chief secretary; I twice served as Hanlin academician; I was then made academician of the Hall of Illuminated Clarity, grand academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and commissioner of the Taewei Palace; I again served as grand academician of the Hongwen Hall; I also served as commissioner for salt and iron transport of all circuits, commissioner for the southern suburbs grand rites, and imperial tomb commissioner for Emperors Mingzong and Gaozu of Jin; I was again appointed military governor of the Dingguo Army and commissioner for observation and disposition in Tong Prefecture; once I served as commissioner of the Changchun Palace; and I was again appointed military governor of the Wusheng Army and commissioner for observation and disposition in Deng, Sui, Jun, Fang, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 官自攝幽府參軍、試大理評事、檢校尚書祠部郎中兼侍御史、檢校吏部郎中兼御史中丞、檢校太尉、同中書門下平章事、檢校太師、兼侍中，又授檢校太師、兼中書令。

translations.literal: As for my titles, I began as acting military adjutant of the You prefecture headquarters, probationary reviewer at the Court of Judicial Review, honorary director of the Ministry of Rites in the Department of State Affairs concurrent with censor, honorary director in the Ministry of Personnel concurrent with vice censor-in-chief, honorary Grand Commandant, Grand Chancellor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, honorary Grand Preceptor concurrent with Palace Attendant, and was again appointed honorary Grand Preceptor concurrent with Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In title I began as acting military adjutant of the Youzhou headquarters, probationary reviewer at the Court of Judicial Review, honorary director of the Ministry of Rites in the Department of State Affairs with concurrent appointment as censor, honorary director in the Ministry of Personnel with concurrent appointment as vice censor-in-chief, honorary Grand Commandant, Grand Chancellor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, honorary Grand Preceptor with concurrent appointment as Palace Attendant, and was again appointed honorary Grand Preceptor with concurrent appointment as Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 正官自行臺中書舍人，再為戶部侍郎，轉兵部侍郎、中書侍郎，再為門下侍郎、刑部吏部尚書、右僕射，三為司空，兩在中書，一守本官，又授司徒、兼侍中，賜私門十六戟，又授太尉、兼侍中，又授戎太傅，又授漢太師。

translations.literal: In regular office I began as acting drafter in the Secretariat, twice served as Vice Minister of Revenue, was transferred to Vice Minister of War and Vice Director of the Secretariat, again served as Vice Director of the Chancellery, Minister of Justice, and Minister of Personnel, and Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; thrice I served as Minister of Works, twice in the Secretariat, once keeping my original office; I was again appointed Minister of Education concurrent with Palace Attendant, granted sixteen halberds at my private gate, again appointed Grand Commandant concurrent with Palace Attendant, again appointed Grand Preceptor of the Rong, and again appointed Grand Preceptor of Han.
translations.idiomatic: In regular appointment I began as acting drafter in the Secretariat, twice served as Vice Minister of Revenue, was transferred to Vice Minister of War and Vice Director of the Secretariat, and again served as Vice Director of the Chancellery, Minister of Justice, Minister of Personnel, and Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; I thrice served as Minister of Works, twice in the Secretariat and once while retaining my original office; I was again appointed Minister of Education with concurrent appointment as Palace Attendant and granted sixteen halberds at my private gate; I was again appointed Grand Commandant with concurrent appointment as Palace Attendant, then Grand Preceptor of the Rong, and then Grand Preceptor of Han.

sentences.zh: 爵自開國男至開國公、魯國公，再封秦國公、梁國公、燕國公、齊國公。

translations.literal: As for my nobility titles, I began as Opening Baron and rose through Opening Duke and Lord of Lu, and was again enfeoffed as Lord of Qin, Lord of Liang, Lord of Yan, and Lord of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In nobility I rose from Opening Baron through Opening Duke and Lord of Lu, and was again enfeoffed as Lord of Qin, Lord of Liang, Lord of Yan, and Lord of Qi.

sentences.zh: 食邑自三百戶至一萬一千戶，食實封自一百戶至一千八百戶。

translations.literal: As for my fief households, they rose from three hundred households to eleven thousand households, and actual fief households from one hundred to eighteen hundred.
translations.idiomatic: My registered fief rose from three hundred households to eleven thousand, and actual fief households from one hundred to eighteen hundred.

sentences.zh: 勛自柱國至上柱國。

translations.literal: As for my orders of merit, I rose from Pillar of the State to Supreme Pillar of the State.
translations.idiomatic: In order of merit I rose from Pillar of the State to Supreme Pillar of the State.

sentences.zh: 功臣名自經邦致理翊贊功臣至守正崇德保邦致理功臣、安時處順守義崇靜功臣、崇仁保德寧邦翊聖功臣。

translations.literal: As for my merit-subject titles, I began as Merit Subject Who Brings Order to the Realm and Supports Governance, and rose through Merit Subject Who Upholds Rectitude and Esteems Virtue in Preserving the Realm and Bringing Order, Merit Subject Who Keeps the Times and Stands with the Flow in Upholding Righteousness and Promoting Tranquility, and Merit Subject Who Honors Benevolence and Preserves Virtue in Settling the Realm and Supporting the Sage.
translations.idiomatic: In merit-subject title I rose from Merit Subject Who Brings Order to the Realm and Supports Governance through Merit Subject Who Upholds Rectitude and Esteems Virtue in Preserving the Realm and Bringing Order, Merit Subject Who Keeps the Times and Stands with the Flow in Upholding Righteousness and Promoting Tranquility, and Merit Subject Who Honors Benevolence and Preserves Virtue in Settling the Realm and Supporting the Sage.

sentences.zh: 先娶故德州戶掾褚諱濆女，早亡，後娶故景州弓高縣孫明府諱師禮女，累封蜀國夫人。

translations.literal: I first married the daughter of the late household clerk of Dezhou, Chu, taboo name Fen; she died young. Later I married the daughter of the late magistrate of Gonggao County in Jingzhou, Sun, taboo name Shili; she was repeatedly enfeoffed as Lady of the State of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: My first wife was the daughter of the late household clerk of Dezhou Chu, taboo name Fen; she died young. I later married the daughter of the late magistrate of Gonggao in Jingzhou Sun, taboo name Shili, who was successively enfeoffed as Lady of the State of Shu.

sentences.zh: 亡長子平，自秘書郎授右拾遺、工部度支員外郎；

translations.literal: My deceased eldest son Ping, from Secretary of the Secretariat was appointed Right Reminder and Vice Director of Revenue in the Ministry of Works;
translations.idiomatic: My late eldest son Ping rose from Secretary to Right Reminder and Vice Director of Revenue in the Ministry of Works;

sentences.zh: 次子吉，自秘書省校書郎授膳部金部職方員外郎、屯田郎中；

translations.literal: My second son Ji, from Proofreader of the Secretariat was appointed Vice Director of Provisions, of the Gold Bureau, and of the Bureau of Appointments in the Ministry of Revenue, and Director of Domains;
translations.idiomatic: My second son Ji rose from Secretariat proofreader to Vice Director in Provisions, the Gold Bureau, and the Bureau of Appointments, and Director of Domains;

sentences.zh: 第三亡子可，自秘書省正字授殿中丞、工部戶部員外郎；

translations.literal: My third deceased son Ke, from Rectifier of the Secretariat was appointed Palace Vice Director and Vice Director in the Ministries of Works and Revenue;
translations.idiomatic: My third son Ke, now deceased, rose from Secretariat rectifier to Palace Vice Director and Vice Director in the Ministries of Works and Revenue;

sentences.zh: 第四子幼亡；

translations.literal: My fourth son died in youth;
translations.idiomatic: My fourth son died in childhood;

sentences.zh: 第五子義，自秘書郎改授銀青光祿大夫、檢校國子祭酒兼御史中丞，充定國軍衙內都指揮使，職罷改授朝散大夫、左春坊太子司議郎、授太常丞；

translations.literal: My fifth son Yi, from Secretary was transferred and appointed Grand Master with Silver-Green Seal and Glorious Emolument, Honorary Director of the Directorate of Education with concurrent appointment as Vice Censor-in-Chief, and served as commander-in-chief of the Dingguo Army headquarters; when his post ended he was transferred and appointed Court Gentleman for Disseminating Merit, Left Spring Palace Aide for the Heir Apparent and Remonstrating Officer, and then appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices;
translations.idiomatic: My fifth son Yi rose from Secretary to Grand Master with Silver-Green Seal and Glorious Emolument, Honorary Director of the Directorate of Education with concurrent appointment as Vice Censor-in-Chief, and served as commander-in-chief of the Dingguo Army headquarters; after leaving that office he was made Court Gentleman for Disseminating Merit and Remonstrating Officer in the Left Spring Palace of the Heir Apparent, then Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices;

sentences.zh: 第六子正，自協律郎改授銀青光祿大夫、檢校國子祭酒兼御史中丞，充定國軍節度使，職罷改授朝散大夫、太僕丞。

translations.literal: My sixth son Zheng, from Master of Harmonies was transferred and appointed Grand Master with Silver-Green Seal and Glorious Emolument, Honorary Director of the Directorate of Education with concurrent appointment as Vice Censor-in-Chief, and served as military governor of the Dingguo Army; when his post ended he was transferred and appointed Court Gentleman for Disseminating Merit and Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: My sixth son Zheng rose from Master of Harmonies to Grand Master with Silver-Green Seal and Glorious Emolument, Honorary Director of the Directorate of Education with concurrent appointment as Vice Censor-in-Chief, and served as military governor of the Dingguo Army; after leaving that office he was made Court Gentleman for Disseminating Merit and Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 長女適故兵部崔侍郎諱衍子太僕少卿名絢，封萬年縣君；

translations.literal: My eldest daughter was married to the son of the late Vice Minister of War Cui, taboo name Yan—Grand Vice Director of the Imperial Stud, name Xuan; she was enfeoffed as Lady of Wannian County;
translations.idiomatic: My eldest daughter married the son of the late Vice Minister of War Cui Yan—Vice Director of the Imperial Stud Xuan—and was enfeoffed as Lady of Wannian County;

sentences.zh: 三女子早亡。

translations.literal: Three daughters died young.
translations.idiomatic: Three daughters died young.

sentences.zh: 二孫幼亡。

translations.literal: Two grandsons died in youth.
translations.idiomatic: Two grandsons died in childhood.

sentences.zh: 唐長興二年敕，瀛州景城縣莊來蘇鄉改為元輔鄉，朝漢裏為孝行裏。

translations.literal: By Tang edict of the second year of Changxing, Laisu Township at the Jingcheng estate in Ying Prefecture was renamed Yuanfu Township, and Chaohan Ward was renamed Xiaoxing Ward.
translations.idiomatic: A Tang edict of the second year of Changxing renamed Laisu Township at the Jingcheng estate in Ying Prefecture as Yuanfu Township and Chaohan Ward as Xiaoxing Ward.

sentences.zh: 洛南莊貫河南府洛陽縣三州鄉靈臺裏，奉晉天福五年敕，三州鄉改為上相鄉，靈臺裏改為中臺裏，時守司徒、兼侍中；

translations.literal: The Luonan estate lay within Sanzhou Township and Lingtai Ward of Luoyang County, Henan Prefecture. By Later Jin edict of the fifth year of Tianfu, Sanzhou Township was renamed Shangxiang Township and Lingtai Ward was renamed Zhongtai Ward; at the time I held the posts of Minister of Education concurrent with Palace Attendant;
translations.idiomatic: The Luonan estate lay in Sanzhou Township and Lingtai Ward of Luoyang, Henan. A Later Jin edict of the fifth year of Tianfu renamed Sanzhou as Shangxiang Township and Lingtai as Zhongtai Ward, while I was serving as Minister of Education with concurrent appointment as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 又奉八年敕，上相鄉改為太尉鄉，中臺裏改為侍中裏，時守太尉、兼侍中。

translations.literal: Again by edict of the eighth year, Shangxiang Township was renamed Grand Marshal Township and Zhongtai Ward was renamed Palace Attendant Ward; at the time I held the posts of Grand Marshal concurrent with Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict of the eighth year renamed Shangxiang as Grand Marshal Township and Zhongtai as Palace Attendant Ward, while I was Grand Marshal with concurrent appointment as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 靜思本末，慶及存亡，蓋自國恩，盡從家法，承訓誨之旨，關教化之源，在孝於家，在忠於國，口無不道之言，門無不義之貨。

translations.literal: Reflecting quietly on the beginning and end of things, my fortune reaches the living and the dead; it all comes from the grace of the state and fully follows the family code. Upholding the aim of instruction and admonition touches the source of transformation and edification: to be filial within the family and loyal to the state, with no improper words spoken and no unrighteous goods at my gate.
translations.idiomatic: When I quietly consider the course of my life, the blessings that reach both living and dead come entirely from the grace of the state and the discipline of our family code. Holding to instruction and admonition touches the source of moral transformation: filial piety at home, loyalty to the state, no improper speech, and no unrighteous wealth at my gate.

sentences.zh: 所願者下不欺於地，中不欺於人，上不欺於天，以三不欺為素。

translations.literal: What I aspire to is not to deceive the earth below, not to deceive people in the middle, and not to deceive Heaven above—I take these three principles of not deceiving as my constant standard.
translations.idiomatic: I aspire never to deceive earth below, people around me, or Heaven above, and I make these three principles of honesty my constant standard.

sentences.zh: 賤如是，貴如是，長如是，老如是，事親、事君、事長、臨人之道，曠蒙天恕，累經難而獲多福，曾陷蕃而歸中華，非人之謀，是天之祐。

translations.literal: Lowly thus, exalted thus, growing thus, aging thus—the way of serving parents, serving the ruler, serving elders, and facing people—I have long received Heaven's forgiveness, passed through many hardships yet gained much fortune; I once fell into barbarian captivity and returned to China; it was not human scheming but Heaven's protection.
translations.idiomatic: In low station or high, in youth or old age, in serving parents, serving the ruler, serving elders, and facing others—I have long enjoyed Heaven's indulgence, endured many hardships yet received much blessing, and once fell into barbarian hands yet returned to China; this was not human design but Heaven's protection.

sentences.zh: 六合之內有幸者，百歲之後有歸所。

translations.literal: Those who find fortune within the six directions have a place to return to after a hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Those blessed within the four quarters of the world will have a place to return to after a hundred years.

sentences.zh: 無以珠玉含，當以時服斂，以籧篨葬，及擇不食之地而葬焉，以不及於古人故。

translations.literal: Do not place pearls and jade in my mouth; I should be laid out in the garments of the season, buried in a bamboo mat coffin, and interred on ground chosen so as not to harm the living—I do so because I do not match the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: Do not fill my mouth with pearls and jade; lay me out in garments of the season, bury me in a bamboo-mat coffin, and choose ground that does not take from the living—for I do not measure up to the ancients.

sentences.zh: 祭以特羊，戒殺生也，當以不害命之物祭。

translations.literal: Sacrifice with a single ram; this restrains killing for food. Offerings should use things that do not harm life.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice with a single ram, as a restraint against slaughter; offerings should be things that do not take life.

sentences.zh: 無立神道碑，以三代墳前不獲立碑故。

translations.literal: Do not erect a spirit-way stele, because in the Three Dynasties no stele was allowed before tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Do not set up a spirit-way stele, because no stele was placed before tombs in the Three Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 無請謚號，以無德故。

translations.literal: Do not request a posthumous title, because I have no virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Do not request a posthumous title, for I lack virtue.

sentences.zh: 又念自賓佐至王佐及領藩鎮時，或有微益於國之事節，皆形於公籍。

translations.literal: I also recall that from the time I served as a client's aide to a king's aide, and when I held border commands, any matters of slight benefit to the state were all recorded in the public registers.
translations.idiomatic: I also recall that from my days as a staff officer and chief minister through my border commands, any matter of slight benefit to the state was recorded in the official registers.

sentences.zh: 所著文章篇詠，因多事散失外，收拾得者，編於家集，其間見其志，知之者，罪之者，未知眾寡矣。

translations.literal: As for the essays and poems I composed, apart from many lost through the turmoil of events, whatever could be gathered has been compiled in a family collection. Whether those who discern my intent and those who condemn it are many or few, I do not know.
