translations.idiomatic: Of the essays and poems I wrote, many were lost in the turmoil of events; what could be recovered has been compiled in a family collection. How many read my intent with understanding and how many condemn it, I do not know.

sentences.zh: 有莊、有宅、有群書，有三子可以襲其業。

translations.literal: I have estates, a dwelling, and many books, and three sons who can carry on my work.
translations.idiomatic: I have estates, a home, and many books, and three sons who can carry on my work.

sentences.zh: 於此日五盥，日三省，尚猶日知其所亡，月無忘其所能。

translations.literal: On this day I wash five times; thrice daily I examine myself; I still daily learn what I lack, and monthly do not forget what I can do.
translations.idiomatic: Each day I wash five times and thrice examine myself; I still learn each day what I lack, and each month do not forget what I can do.

sentences.zh: 為子、為弟、為人臣、為師長、為夫、為父，有子、有猶子、有孫，奉身即有餘矣。

translations.literal: As son, younger brother, minister, teacher and elder, husband, and father, with sons, with a nephew-son, and with grandsons—in sustaining myself I already have more than enough.
translations.idiomatic: As son, younger brother, minister, teacher and elder, husband, and father, with sons, a nephew-son, and grandsons, I already have more than enough in the way I have lived.

sentences.zh: 為時乃不足，不足者何？

translations.literal: For the age, however, it is not enough. What is it that is not enough?
translations.idiomatic: But for the age it is not enough. What is not enough?

sentences.zh: 不能為大君致一統、定八方，誠有愧於歷職歷官，何以答乾坤之施。

translations.literal: Unable for the great lord to bring unity and settle the eight directions, truly I feel shame in having held office upon office—how may I answer Heaven and Earth's gifts.
translations.idiomatic: I have failed to bring unity to the realm and settle the empire for my sovereign. I truly feel ashamed of the offices I have held—how can I repay what Heaven and Earth have given me?

sentences.zh: 時開一卷，時飲一杯，食味別聲、被色，老安於當代耶！

translations.literal: At times open one scroll, at times drink one cup; distinguish flavors and sounds, be clothed in color—growing old secure in the present age, indeed!
translations.idiomatic: At times I open a book; at times I drink a cup. I savor food, enjoy music, and clothe myself in finery—growing old content with this age, indeed!

sentences.zh: 老而自樂，何樂如之！

translations.literal: Growing old yet finding joy in oneself—what joy could match this!
translations.idiomatic: To grow old and find joy in oneself—what greater joy could there be!

sentences.zh: 時乾祐三年朱明月長樂老序云。

translations.literal: At the time—in Qianyou year 3—Zhu Mingyue's Preface to a Contented Elder says.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the Preface to a Contented Elder, written at the time in Qianyou year 3 by Zhu Mingyue.

sentences.zh: 及太祖平內難，議立徐州節度使劉赟為漢嗣，遣道與秘書監趙上交、樞密直學士王度等往迎之。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor quelled internal troubles, they resolved to install Liu Yun, military governor of Xuzhou, as heir to the Later Han, and sent Dao with Director of the Secretariat Zhao Shangjiao, Privy Council academician Wang Du, and others to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: After the Founding Emperor quelled the internal crisis, the court resolved to install Liu Yun, military governor of Xuzhou, as heir to the Later Han and sent Feng Dao with Zhao Shangjiao, director of the Secretariat, Wang Du, privy council academician, and others to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 道尋與赟自徐赴汴，行至宋州，會澶州軍變。

translations.literal: Soon Dao and Yun set out from Xu for Bian; reaching Songzhou, they encountered the military mutiny at Chanzho.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao and Liu Yun soon set out from Xuzhou for Bianliang. When they reached Songzhou, they encountered the mutiny of the troops at Chanzho.

sentences.zh: 樞密使王峻遣郭崇領兵至，屯於衙門外，時道與上交等宿於衙內。

translations.literal: Privy Commissioner Wang Jun sent Guo Chong leading troops to arrive; they encamped outside the yamen gate. At the time Dao and Shangjiao and the others lodged inside the yamen.
translations.idiomatic: Privy commissioner Wang Jun sent Guo Chong with troops, who encamped outside the yamen gate. Feng Dao and Zhao Shangjiao and the others were lodging inside.

sentences.zh: 是日，赟率左右甲士闔門登樓，詰崇所自，崇言太祖已副推戴。

translations.literal: That day Yun led armed guards of his suite, closed the gate and mounted the tower, questioned where Guo Chong had come from; Chong said the Founding Emperor had already received the acclamation.
translations.idiomatic: That day Liu Yun led his armored guards, shut the gate, and mounted the tower to question Guo Chong's origin. Chong replied that the Founding Emperor had already been acclaimed.

sentences.zh: 左右知其事變，以為道所賣，皆欲殺道等以自快。

translations.literal: His attendants, knowing of the turn of events, believed Dao had betrayed them, and all wished to kill Dao and the others to satisfy themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When his attendants learned what had happened, they believed Feng Dao had betrayed them and all wanted to kill him and his companions to vent their rage.

sentences.zh: 趙上交與王度聞之，皆惶怖不知所為，惟道偃仰自適，略無懼色，尋亦獲免焉。

translations.literal: Zhao Shangjiao and Wang Du heard of it; both were fearful and did not know what to do; only Dao lay back at ease, showing no fear at all, and soon they were also spared.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shangjiao and Wang Du were terrified and did not know what to do. Only Feng Dao reclined at ease without the slightest sign of fear, and in the end they all escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 道微時嘗賦詩云：「終聞海嶽歸明主，未省乾坤陷吉人。

translations.literal: When Dao was still obscure he once composed a poem: "In the end I hear seas and mountains return to a bright lord; I do not yet see Heaven and Earth trap the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: In his early days Feng Dao once wrote a poem: "In the end I hear that seas and mountains return to a wise ruler; I have never seen Heaven and Earth destroy a good man.

sentences.zh: 」至是其言驗矣。

translations.literal: " At last his words were fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: " And so at last his words came true.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （《青箱雜記》載馮道詩全篇云：莫為危時便愴神，前程往往有期因，終聞海嶽歸明主，未省乾坤陷吉人。

translations.literal: (Green Box Miscellany records Feng Dao's whole poem: Do not in perilous times at once grow sorrowful in spirit; the road ahead often has its appointed cause; in the end I hear seas and mountains return to a bright lord; I do not yet see Heaven and Earth trap the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: (Green Box Miscellany records Feng Dao's complete poem: Do not let perilous times at once break your spirit; the road ahead often has its appointed cause; in the end I hear that seas and mountains return to a wise ruler; I have never seen Heaven and Earth destroy a good man.

sentences.zh: 道德幾時曾去世，舟車何處不通津，但教方寸無諸惡，狼虎叢中也立身。）〉

translations.literal: When has worth ever perished from the world? Where have boats and carts not reached a ford? Only teach the inch-square heart to harbor no evil, and even amid wolves and tigers one may stand upright.)〉
translations.idiomatic: When has a worthy man ever truly left the world? Where have boats and carts not found a crossing? Keep your heart free of evil, and even among wolves and tigers you may stand upright.)]

sentences.zh: 廣順初，復拜太師、中書令，太祖甚重之，每進對不以名呼。

translations.literal: Early in Guangshun, he was again appointed Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat; the Founding Emperor greatly valued him and, whenever he came to audience, did not call him by name.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangshun era he was again appointed grand preceptor and director of the Secretariat. The Founding Emperor held him in high esteem and never addressed him by name when he came to audience.

sentences.zh: 及太祖崩，世宗以道為山陵使。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor died, Shizong appointed Dao mountain tomb commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor died, Emperor Shizong appointed Feng Dao commissioner for the imperial tomb.

sentences.zh: 會河東劉崇入寇，世宗召大臣議欲親征，道諫止之，世宗因言：「唐初，天下草寇蜂起，並是太宗親平之。

translations.literal: When Liu Chong of Hedong invaded, Shizong summoned ministers to discuss a personal campaign; Dao remonstrated and stopped it. Shizong then said: "Early in Tang, bandits rose like hornets throughout the realm—all were personally pacified by Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Chong of Hedong invaded, Shizong summoned his ministers to discuss a personal campaign. Feng Dao remonstrated against it, whereupon Shizong said: "In early Tang, bandits rose everywhere like hornets, and Taizong personally pacified them all.

sentences.zh: 」道奏曰：「陛下得如太宗否？

translations.literal: " Dao memorialized: "Can Your Majesty be like Taizong?
translations.idiomatic: " Feng Dao replied: "Can Your Majesty be like Taizong?

sentences.zh: 」世宗怒曰：「馮道何相少也！

translations.literal: " Shizong angrily said: "How little does Feng Dao think of his minister!
translations.idiomatic: " Shizong angrily said: "How little respect Feng Dao shows his emperor!

sentences.zh: 」乃罷。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the discussion was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: " With that the audience ended.

sentences.zh: 及世宗親征，不及扈從，留道奉太祖山陵。

translations.literal: When Shizong personally campaigned, Dao could not accompany him as guard; he was left to tend the Founding Emperor's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong marched in person, Feng Dao could not accompany him and was left behind to oversee the Founding Emperor's tomb.

sentences.zh: 時道已抱疾。

translations.literal: At the time Dao was already ill.
translations.idiomatic: By then Feng Dao was already ill.

sentences.zh: 及山陵禮畢，奉神主歸舊宮，未及祔廟，一夕薨於其第，時顯德元年四月十七日也，享年七十有三。

translations.literal: When the tomb rites were complete, he escorted the spirit tablet back to the old palace; before it could be enshrined in the ancestral temple, one evening he died at his residence—Xiande year 1, the seventeenth day of the fourth month; he enjoyed years seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: When the tomb rites were finished, he escorted the spirit tablet back to the old palace. Before it could be enshrined in the ancestral temple, he died one evening at his residence on the seventeenth day of the fourth month of Xiande year 1, at the age of seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 世宗聞之，輟視朝三日，冊贈尚書令，追封瀛王，謚曰文懿。

translations.literal: Shizong heard of it, suspended court audiences for three days, bestowed by edict the title Director of the Department of State Affairs, posthumously enfeoffed him as Prince of Ying, posthumous name Wenyi.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong heard the news, he suspended court for three days, posthumously bestowed on him the title of director of the Department of State Affairs, enfeoffed him as Prince of Ying, and gave him the posthumous name Wenyi.

sentences.zh: 道歷任四朝，三入中書，在相位二十餘年，以持重鎮俗為己任，未嘗以片簡擾於諸侯，平生甚廉儉。

translations.literal: Dao served four dynasties, thrice entered the Secretariat, held the chancellorship for more than twenty years, took steady governance to settle custom as his charge, never with a scrap of paper troubled the feudatories, and in life was very frugal.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao served four dynasties, entered the Secretariat three times, and held the chancellorship for more than twenty years. He made steady governance and the settling of custom his duty, never troubling the regional lords with so much as a note, and lived his life in great frugality.

sentences.zh: 逮至末年，閨庭之內，稍徇奢靡，其子吉，尤恣狂蕩，道不能制，識者以其不終令譽，鹹嘆惜之。

translations.literal: Reaching his final years, within the inner household he slightly indulged extravagance; his son Ji especially gave free rein to wild excess; Dao could not control him; the knowing, because he did not finish with fine reputation, all sighed in regret.
translations.idiomatic: In his final years his household grew somewhat extravagant. His son Ji was especially wild and unrestrained, and Feng Dao could not restrain him. Those who knew him sighed that he had not preserved his good name to the end.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （《五代史補》：馮道之鎮同州也，有酒務吏乞以家財修夫子廟，道以狀付判官參詳其事。

translations.literal: (Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: When Feng Dao governed Tongzhou, a wine-office clerk asked to repair the Confucius temple with his family wealth; Dao handed the petition to the judicial assistant for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: (Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: When Feng Dao was military governor of Tongzhou, a clerk in the wine monopoly asked to repair the Confucius temple with his family fortune. Feng Dao forwarded the petition to the judicial assistant for review.

sentences.zh: 判官素滑稽，因以一絕書判後云：「荊棘森森繞杏壇，儒官高貴盡偷安，若教酒務修夫子，覺我慚惶也大難。

translations.literal: The judicial assistant was by nature a wit; he therefore wrote a quatrain after the judgment: "Thorns stand thick around the apricot altar; Confucian officials, high and noble, all steal ease—if a wine-office clerk repairs Confucius, I feel shame and alarm—how hard!
translations.idiomatic: The judicial assistant was a wit by nature and wrote a quatrain on the back of the judgment: "Thorns stand thick around the apricot altar; lofty Confucian officials all live in ease. If a wine-office clerk repairs Confucius's temple, how hard it is not to feel ashamed!

sentences.zh: 」道覽之有愧色，因出俸重創之。

translations.literal: " Dao read it and showed an ashamed countenance; he therefore donated his salary and rebuilt it at great cost.
translations.idiomatic: " When Feng Dao read it his face showed shame, and he paid for a major rebuilding out of his own salary.

sentences.zh: 馮瀛王道之在中書也，有舉子李導投贄所業，馮相見之，戲謂曰：「老夫名道，其來久矣，加以累居相府，秀才不可謂不知，然亦名導，於禮可乎？

translations.literal: When Prince of Ying Feng Dao was in the Secretariat, an examination candidate Li Dao presented his work for review; the Minister Feng saw him and jestingly said: "This old man is named Dao—it has been so a long time; moreover having repeatedly held the chancellory, scholar, you cannot be said not to know—yet you also are named Dao—in propriety is that acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Ying Feng Dao was at the Secretariat, a candidate named Li Dao submitted his examination work. Feng Dao saw him and said in jest: "This old man's name is Dao, and has been so for a long time. Having served repeatedly as chancellor, you cannot claim not to know that. Yet your name is also Dao—is that proper?

sentences.zh: 」李抗聲對曰：「相公是無寸底道字，小子有寸底導字，何謂不可也！

translations.literal: " Li replied in a loud voice: "The Minister's Dao character has no inch at the bottom; this young man's Dao character has an inch at the bottom—why should it not be acceptable!
translations.idiomatic: " Li Dao answered boldly: "Your Excellency's Dao is the character without an inch at the bottom; this student's Dao is the character with an inch at the bottom. Why should it not be acceptable!

sentences.zh: 」公笑曰：「老夫不惟名無寸，諸事亦無寸，吾子可謂知人矣。

translations.literal: " The Minister laughed and said: "This old man not only has no inch in his name—in all affairs too I have no inch. You, sir, may be called one who knows men.
translations.idiomatic: " Feng Dao laughed and said: "This old man not only has no inch in his name—in all matters I have no inch either. You may truly be called one who knows men.

sentences.zh: 」了無怒色。

translations.literal: " He showed not the slightest anger.
translations.idiomatic: " He showed no anger at all.

sentences.zh: 馮吉，瀛王道之子，能彈琵琶，以皮為弦，世宗嘗令彈於御前，深欣善之，因號其琵琶曰「繞殿雷」也。

translations.literal: Feng Ji, son of Prince of Ying Feng Dao, could play the pipa with leather strings; Shizong once had him play before the throne, deeply delighted and pleased with it, and therefore named his pipa "Thunder Wrapping the Hall."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ji, son of Prince of Ying Feng Dao, could play the pipa with leather strings. Shizong once had him perform before the throne, was deeply pleased, and named his pipa "Hall-Ringing Thunder."

sentences.zh: 道以其惰業，每加譴責，而吉攻之愈精，道益怒，凡與客飲，必使庭立而彈之，曲罷或賜以束帛，命背負之，然後致謝。

translations.literal: Dao because of his idle occupation repeatedly rebuked and chastised him, yet Ji practiced ever more finely; Dao grew ever angrier. Whenever he drank with guests he always made Ji stand in the courtyard and play; when the piece ended he sometimes rewarded him with bolts of silk and ordered him to carry them on his back—only then to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao rebuked him constantly for this idle pursuit, but Ji practiced ever more diligently, which only angered his father further. Whenever Feng Dao entertained guests, he made Ji stand in the courtyard and play. When the piece ended he sometimes rewarded him with bolts of silk and ordered him to carry them on his back before he might give thanks.

sentences.zh: 道自以為戒勖極矣，吉未能悛改，既而益自若。

translations.literal: Dao considered his admonition and encouragement extreme; Ji could not reform, and thereafter grew ever more at ease with himself.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao thought he had admonished and disciplined him to the utmost, but Ji would not reform and only grew more self-assured.

sentences.zh: 道度無可奈何，嘆曰：「百工之司藝而身賤，理使然也。

translations.literal: Dao judged there was nothing to be done and sighed: "Craftsmen who master an art yet remain base in station—it is the way of things.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing there was nothing to be done, Feng Dao sighed: "Craftsmen who master an art yet remain low in station—that is simply the way of things.

sentences.zh: 此子不過太常少卿耳。

translations.literal: This son will be nothing more than Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Rites.
translations.idiomatic: This son will rise no higher than vice director of the Court of Imperial Rites.

sentences.zh: 」其後果終於此。）〉

translations.literal: " In the end he indeed ended in that office.)〉
translations.idiomatic: " In the end that is exactly where he ended.)]

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：道之履行，郁有古人之風；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Dao's conduct and integrity had abundantly the air of ancients;
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: In conduct and integrity Feng Dao richly possessed the spirit of the ancients;

sentences.zh: 道之宇量，深得大臣之禮。

translations.literal: Dao's breadth of character deeply accorded with the rites of a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: in breadth of character he deeply fulfilled the duties of a great minister.

sentences.zh: 然而事四朝，相六帝，可得為忠乎！

translations.literal: Yet having served four dynasties and been chancellor to six emperors—can this be called loyalty!
translations.idiomatic: Yet to have served four dynasties and been chancellor to six emperors—can that be called loyalty?

sentences.zh: 夫一女二夫，人之不幸，況於再三者哉！

translations.literal: For one woman to have two husbands is a person's misfortune—how much more when it happens thrice or more!
translations.idiomatic: For one woman to have two husbands is a misfortune—how much more when it happens again and again!

sentences.zh: 所以飾終之典，不得謚為文貞、文忠者，蓋謂此也。

translations.literal: Therefore in the rites honoring the dead he was not given the posthumous names Wen Zhen or Wen Zhong—it is because of this.
translations.idiomatic: That is why, in the rites honoring the dead, he was not given the posthumous names Wen Zhen or Wen Zhong.
